source.title: How Predictable Are Large Language Model Capabilities? A Case Study on BIG-bench
source.authors: Qinyuan Ye; Harvey Yiyun Fu; Xiang Ren; Robin Jia

record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream-performance predictability with regression models and BIG-bench records, rather than fitting the original power laws to held-out pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The study predicts normalized BIG-bench task scores from model family, parameter count, task, and number of in-context examples. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy, fit the original loss power laws, or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. The cited scaling-law results are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study predicts BIG-bench downstream scores from model family, parameter count, task and shots with learned regressors, not power laws. It reports how predictable downstream performance is, including holding out the largest GPT-3 and PaLM models. This bears on V6. It reports no pretraining loss, allocation or architecture-shape results.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors also conclude that emergent tasks are 'not entirely unpredictable' though harder to predict. They also report that BIG-bench Lite/Hard are suboptimal subsets for recovering full-benchmark performance, while diverse, high-value subsets work better.
record.recipe_differences: Uses matrix completion, tree-based methods, and MLP predictors over BIG-bench task scores; it does not fit power laws to held-out pretraining loss or estimate compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Prediction performance changes with the train-test split, whether the task/model groups are represented in training, and whether information from the test distribution is used for model selection or training. The authors also report that larger-model groups are harder to predict.

fits_no_version.finding: Extrapolating to more in-context examples (train on 0–2 shots, test on 3 shots) gives R2 0.93 in the strict setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream performance is predictable across numbers of in-context examples.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The dataset covers only six model families and BIG-bench tasks, and the authors caution against generalizing to real-world task distributions. Most experiments are interpolation settings. The extrapolation results are preliminary; strict larger-model prediction is weak for PaLM 535B. Group-wise R2 comparisons have metric limitations noted by the authors.
record.rows_left_out: Table 6 RMSE, task-average Pearson, and task-average Kendall results were not separately recorded; the R2 metric is the principal measure used for the prediction findings. Other textual group-wise results and plotted task-level examples were not separately extracted where exact outcomes were not stated. The paper also reports small-bench selection results, which do not measure downstream performance predictability itself.

untested.parts: No power laws fitted to loss and extrapolated.
No depth/width/shape comparisons at fixed size.
No other modalities or training regimes.
No relation of downstream scores to pretraining loss. No explicit scaling-curve fits. Only BIG-bench and six model families.
No comparison of fitted exponents or fitting choices.

missing.what: Bar values for the single-group vs multi-group R2 by parameter bucket (only the trend is stated in the text)

record.verdict_notes: Predictions come from learned regressors that use cross-model and cross-task information, not scale-only trend fits. High interpolation R2 therefore says more about shared structure in the records than about scaling curves. The strict extrapolation rows (S1) are the most direct V6 evidence. S2 and S3 leak test-distribution data.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss and its power-law relationship with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Power laws fitted on small runs predicting held-out loss on much larger runs. The study has limited downstream-score extrapolation experiments using learned predictors, not fitted power laws.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and architecture at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
Tests predictability of BIG-bench downstream task scores, not a general relationship to pretraining loss or downstream performance across other benchmarks and settings.
Does not compare fitted power-law exponents, compute-optimal allocations, or power-law fitting choices.

relation.reason: The study directly evaluates prediction accuracy across random, grouped and extrapolation holdouts.

tranche.reason: Learned regressors test downstream performance predictability using model scale and experiment configurations, a different method aimed at V6.

source_check.notes: The 200B and 535B labels reproduce Appendix C.3/Table 4; Table 2 instead lists GPT-3 up to 175B and PaLM up to 540B. Aggregate score predictability does not establish monotonic improvement or a downstream power law.

statements.correction: Table 4, E2.2, source-labelled PaLM 535B: S1 R²=0.1535; S2 R²=0.5731. Strict model-size extrapolation is weak; V6 verdict for this condition: limits_scope.
statements.problem: The PaLM value and holdout description are correct, but the challenges label overstates this study's evidence: weak positive predictability warrants limits_scope rather than absence or reversal.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Default random split and tested task groups
reader_labels.reason: Prediction is strong on the default split (L1-mlp) and for emergent and non-emergent task aggregates (emergent, nonemergent).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: More challenging splits, larger-model extrapolation, and larger parameter buckets
reader_labels.reason: Prediction weakens under harder data splits and especially strict larger-model extrapolation; larger parameter buckets are reported as harder to predict (L21-mlp, L22-mlp, L3-mlp, LC-mlp, E21-S1, E22-S1, larger-buckets).
